dedupe_keys.name: ci res critical infrastructures resilience enea webgis platform with multi hazard analysis of italian infrastructure

description: CI-RES, Critical Infrastructures RESilience, is a WebGIS platform from ENEA's laboratory for critical infrastructures and essential services for integrated analysis and resilience assessment of infrastructure systems in Italy. When read it listed 104 resources, 82 of them datasets such as weather vigilance bulletins, alongside maps, documents, geostories and dashboards, plus analysis tools for multi-hazard analysis, ground motion from the European Ground Motion Service and weather alerts. A July 2026 paper in Infrastructures by the ENEA team describes the multi-hazard plugin, which combines the Analytical Hierarchy Process with weighted linear combination to score assets against six hazards, earthquakes, floods, landslides, volcanoes, wildfires and tsunamis, with user-set priorities; a national case found about 48 percent of roads, 58 percent of road bridges and viaducts, 46 percent of railways and 66 percent of railway bridges in medium-to-high multi-hazard zones. Coverage is Italy. Format and access: a GeoNode web platform with a public catalogue and an API; some tools need sign-in. Licence: not stated for the platform, the paper is CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: multi-hazard scores depend on expert weights. It supports hazard exposure, resilience and emergency response analysis of Italian networks. A related catalogue record is ENEA's CIPCast decision support system.
